messages:
maria (docs): Hey all — I'm opening a PR to consolidate the localization & region availability notes. Draft here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 :wave:
kevin (eng): nice, I'll skim. Do you need any new endpoint info from infra for APAC regions?
maria (docs): yes please. The table currently lists supported regions but not which deployment modes are available per region (hosted / dedicated / private). Need that added.
ayan (product): For product we want the regions table to show: hosted availability, dedicated availability (yes/no), private install supported (yes/no), and data residency guarantees (Y/N + notes).
kevin (eng): quick note: dedicated in ap-southeast-1 will be beta until May. Also, private on-prem obviously 'depends' but we should mention "on-prem supported — contact sales".
liam (legal): Heads-up — for EU-Germany customers we need an explicit data residency blurb and GDPR processing note. Also ask security to confirm KMS/HSM compliance language.
maria (docs): Good call. I'll add a short GDPR note and link to our compliance page. @kevin can you confirm which regions have KMS-integrated key wrapping?
kevin (eng): KMS integration is available in us-west-2, eu-west-1, and ap-northeast-1 for hosted right now. Dedicated can integrate via customer KMS if provisioned; Private depends on customer's KMS/HSM. I'll add a snippet to the PR.
docs-bot: Reminder — docs CI will run after you push changes.
maria (docs): Pushing an update in 10m. Plan: add columns to the regions table, add a short data residency FAQ entry, and include a Python SDK snippet showing how to set region and request regional_tenant.
kevin (eng): For the SDK snippet, use this pattern:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(region="eu-west-1", api_key=...)
resp = client.generate("Hello")
```
liam (legal): For the GDPR sentence, suggest: "We may process customer data within the region specified by your tenancy; for EU data residency guarantees please contact sales for contractual terms." We need sign-off from security.
ayan (product): Also add a tiny migration note for customers moving from hosted to dedicated: call out IP allowlist changes and model pinning differences.
maria (docs): I'll draft the migration checklist bullet points. Also thinking about a short change log entry: "Updated regions table (Mar 2026) — added deployment availability and residency notes."
kevin (eng): FYI, when you mention latency SLOs per region, don't hardcode numbers — link to the perf page instead.
maria (docs): Good call. I've left placeholders linking to /docs/performance.
liam (legal): I'll review the GDPR blurb in the PR, ping me once it's up.
docs-bot: PR 789 created by maria: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 — CI queued.
maria (docs): OK pushed. Please leave quick review comments inline. If security or legal flag wording, I'll iterate.
kevin (eng): Reviewing now, small nit: change "data residency" -> "data locality" in one spot because residency has legal implications.
liam (legal): Agree with Kevin. I'll add suggested wording in the PR review.
ayan (product): One more ask: add an explicit note about Private (VPC) deployments: "Customer-managed network and KMS/HSM; audit logs available on request."
maria (docs): Will add. Thanks everyone — hoping to merge after legal + security sign-off.
kevin (eng): I'll add the region/kms table patch in a follow-up commit if needed.
liam (legal): Marking for review — expect comments in the next 24h.
maria (docs): Thanks — marking thread resolved for now. Will re-open if reviewers leave blocking comments. :white_check_mark:
